projects.title: SevSetu
projects.logline: A multilingual generative-AI chatbot that explains government schemes in Bhojpuri, Hindi and English.
projects.problem: Many government notifications are published in English or formal Hindi, so people who speak regional languages like Bhojpuri, or who don’t read well, miss out on schemes meant for them.
projects.solution: Users ask questions in Hindi, Bhojpuri or English and get clear, simple, actionable answers about schemes such as PM Kisan, Atal Pension Yojana and PMAY.
features: Web, browser extension, mobile and desktop apps

projects.title: Recruit AI
projects.logline: An AI interview-prep platform that scores resume–job fit and builds a personal prep plan.
projects.problem: Job seekers don’t know how well their resume fits a role, what questions to expect, or how to prepare. Generic interview advice doesn’t use their own profile or the specific job description.
projects.solution: The user uploads a resume and pastes a job description; Gemini generates a match score, technical and behavioural questions with model answers, skill gaps and a day-wise prep plan. It can also produce a tailored, ATS-friendly resume PDF. JWT login lets users reopen saved reports.
features: Strict processing → success / failed state handling

Gemini API integration for AI-powered analysis

projects.title: Hospital Bill Predictor

projects.solution: Trained and evaluated a Random Forest regression model that predicts hospital expenses from patient data with roughly 90% accuracy, then shipped an interactive Streamlit interface for real-time predictions.

posts.title: How a typical project runs with me: from first call to launch
posts.excerpt: What happens between your first message and a live product: discovery, scope, milestones you approve, and handover.
posts.body:
If you're hiring a freelance developer for the first time, the biggest worry is usually not the code. It's **not knowing what happens next**. Here's the process I follow, so you can judge whether it suits you.

## 1. Discovery call
A short call to understand the goal, who the product is for, and what a successful first version looks like. I'll ask about deadlines, budget range and anything that's already built.

## 2. Written scope and quote
You receive a written proposal with the deliverables, timeline, price and payment schedule. You can accept it online in your client portal. Nothing starts until the scope is agreed.

## 3. Milestones you approve
Work is delivered in small, reviewable milestones. Each one appears in your portal; you either approve it or request changes. The next stage only begins once you're happy.

## 4. Weekly updates
You'll see progress in the portal and get a short update every week, so there are no surprises.

## 5. Launch and handover
I deploy the product, hand over the source code and documentation, and the code is yours once the final invoice is paid.

## Want to talk about your project?
Tell me what you're building using the form on the contact section, and I'll reply within 1–2 working days.
